title: Waiting lists that stopped moving
question: When the taxi medallion waiting list and the condominium lottery were closed, what replaced them, and who gained from the new rule as far as the published records show?
finding: Taxi medallions: free medallions went down a waiting list that held 3,029 people in 2012, by when it was closed to new names; from 2010 the City offered medallions for sale instead. Of 722 medallions now held as purchased, 302 (41.8%) are marked foreclosed, and 302 purchased medallions are held in the name of 2 credit unions, so the buyers are not shown to have gained. Condominium lottery: 199 homes a year won conversion until 2013, when 593 entered buildings lost the last drawing; the fee-based program that replaced it converted 1,915 homes, 1,155 of them in its first year, by eligibility and fee, with no drawing.
how: Taxi: offer letters are counted by year from the archived notices; current medallions by holder type, last sale price and financial status from the transportation agency’s holder file (holder types are the file’s own labels). Condominiums: homes in winning buildings per lottery year; homes converted under the replacement program are read from the table in Public Works’ report of 29 December 2023. Drivers and building owners are counted, never named.
limits: Who gained is only partly visible. The records do not show what sellers received, what the City collected, or which waiting-list members bought. A foreclosed medallion is a loss to its buyer and lender, not proof the rule was wrong when made. The courts: “Appeal Court affirms trial court verdict that City did not breach its contract with credit union in taxi medallion case” For condominiums the records do not link lottery losers to later conversions, so it cannot be said that the same owners moved from the drawing to the paid program. Public Works’ report says the ordinance “established seven application rounds each of which had different eligibility date requirements”; those requirements are not on disk, so who qualified first cannot be stated. Its 2019 update says “no lottery shall take place prior to January 1, 2024” and that the longest suspension would be found by “dividing the total number of units approved for conversion in the ECP by 200 and rounded to the nearest whole number”, added to 2014. No lottery result after 2013 is on disk, so whether drawings resumed is not known here.
